title: Second & Third Conditionals
subtitle: Talk about unreal or unlikely situations, in the present and in the past.
objectives: Form the second conditional for unreal/unlikely present or future situations
Form the third conditional for unreal past situations (things that didn't happen)
Tell the two apart based on time

content.intro: You already know real conditionals (zero and first). Now let's talk about the imaginary: what would happen if things were different, now or in the past.

rules.heading: a) Second conditional — unreal present/future
rules.body:
If + past simple, would + base verb. Used for something imaginary, unlikely, or impossible now.

  • If I won the lottery, I would travel the world. (I probably won't win)
  • If I were you, I would apologize. (I'm not you — imaginary advice)

rules.heading: b) Third conditional — unreal past
rules.body:
If + past perfect, would have + past participle. Used for something that didn't actually happen in the past.

  • If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam. (I didn't study harder, so I didn't pass)
  • If she had left earlier, she wouldn't have missed the train.

examples: If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.
If I were you, I would apologize.
If it rained, we would stay home. (unlikely, hypothetical)
If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
If she had left earlier, she wouldn't have missed the train.
If they had known, they would have helped.

commonMistakes.wrong: If I win the lottery, I would travel the world.
commonMistakes.right: If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.
commonMistakes.why: The "if" clause of the second conditional needs the past simple, not the present.

commonMistakes.wrong: If I was you, I would apologize.
commonMistakes.right: If I were you, I would apologize.
commonMistakes.why: In the second conditional, "were" is used for all subjects (including I/he/she) in this fixed expression.

commonMistakes.wrong: If I had study harder, I would have passed.
commonMistakes.right: If I had studied harder, I would have passed.
commonMistakes.why: The third conditional's "if" clause needs the past perfect (had + past participle).

commonMistakes.wrong: If I had studied harder, I would passed the exam.
commonMistakes.right: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
commonMistakes.why: The result clause of the third conditional needs "would have" + past participle.

exercises.title: Fill in the Blanks
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct second or third conditional form.

items.prompt: If I ___ (win) the lottery, I ___ (travel) the world.
If I ___ (study) harder, I ___ (pass) the exam. (but I didn't study)
If she ___ (leave) earlier, she ___ (not/miss) the train.

items.explanation: "Were" is used for all subjects in this fixed second-conditional expression.

items.prompt: Which sentence describes something that didn't actually happen in the past?
options: If it rains, I will stay home.
If I had known, I would have called you.
If I won the lottery, I would travel.
items.explanation: This is the third conditional — an unreal past situation.

items.prompt: Which sentence describes an unlikely present/future situation?
options: If I were rich, I would buy a house.
If you heat water, it boils.
If I had studied, I would have passed.
items.explanation: This is the second conditional — unreal present/future.

items.incorrect: If I win the lottery, I would travel the world.
answer: If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.
items.explanation: The second conditional's "if" clause needs the past simple.

items.incorrect: If they had known, they would help.
answer: If they had known, they would have helped.
items.explanation: The third conditional's result clause needs "would have" + past participle.

summary: Second conditional: If + past simple, would + base verb — unreal present/future.
Third conditional: If + past perfect, would have + past participle — unreal past (didn't happen).
"Were" (not "was") is standard for all subjects in second-conditional "if I were..." expressions.
